newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir seeks new era in Malaysia-Australia ties.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir seeks new era in Malaysia-Australia ties.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said on Friday he wanted his country and Australia to be rid of misconceptions and prejudices that have strained ties in the last decade.

Mahathir, once sharply critical of Australian policies, said at a banquet attended by visiting Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer that relations between Malaysia and Australia were stronger now than before.

But mistakes of the past should not recur and more academic and cultural exchanges were needed to preserve the current warmth, Mahathir said at a dinner for the Malaysia-Australia University Alumni Convention.
"Despite the ups and downs, relations with Australia have been generally good and in recent years have grown stronger."
Ties were strained in the 1980s when then Australian Prime Minister Bob Hawke called the hanging of two convicted Australian drug traffickers by Malaysia a "barbaric" act.
Relations hit a low in 1993 after then Australian Prime Minister Paul Keating called Mahathir "recalcitrant" for skipping the inaugural Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Seattle.
Over the years, Malaysia has also expressed outrage over what it viewed as unflattering potrayals of itself in film and television presentations by Australians.

For its part, Malaysia has debunked efforts by Australia to be viewed as part of Asia, including joining the annual Asia-Europe summit. Australia is also a major proponent of APEC, to which Malaysia has generally been lukewarm. Both are members.
But late last year, signs emerged that tensions were easing. Keating visited Kuala Lumpur in January and Mahathir visited Australia in March, after Prime Minister John Howard came to power.

Mahathir said on Friday the improvement in ties was reflected in trade, with Australian exports to Malaysia growing by 14.2 percent to 5.3 billion ringgit ($2.12 billion) in 1995 from the previous year. Imports rose 28.2 percent to 3.08 billion ringgit, giving Australia a good surplus, he said.
